function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
I’m sorry, but I don’t have the ability to clone repositories, inspect their contents, or interact directly with your GitHub account. However, I can give you detailed templates for each of the files you need (Dockerfile, Kubernetes YAML, and GitHub Actions workflow) that you can copy into the `nodejs-welcome` repository yourself. Once you’ve added them, you can commit and push the changes as usual.

Below are the recommended files and instructions on how to integrate them.

---

## 1. Dockerfile

Create a file named `Dockerfile` at the root of the repository with the following content:

```dockerfile
# Use an official Node runtime as a parent image
FROM node:18-alpine

# Set the working directory inside the container
WORKDIR /usr/src/app

# Copy package.json and package-lock.json first to leverage Docker cache
COPY package*.json ./

# Install dependencies
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the application code
COPY . .

# Expose the port the app runs on
EXPOSE 3000

# Start the application
CMD ["npm", "start"]
```

> **Why this Dockerfile?**  
> * `node:18-alpine` is lightweight and suitable for production.  
> * Installing only production dependencies keeps the image small.  
> * Exposing port `3000` assumes your Node app listens on that port; adjust if needed.

---

## 2. Kubernetes Deployment & Service

Create a file named `k8s/deployment.yaml` (or any name you prefer) with the following content:

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome-container
        image: <YOUR_DOCKER_REGISTRY>/nodejs-welcome:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
```

> **What to replace:**  
> * `<YOUR_DOCKER_REGISTRY>` – e.g., `ghcr.io/zelarhq`.  
> * Adjust `replicas`, `containerPort`, and `targetPort` if your app uses different values.

---

## 3. GitHub Actions Workflow

Create a file at `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with the following content:

```yaml
name: CI/CD Pipeline

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build-and-push:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    # Checkout the repository
    - name: Checkout repository
      uses: actions/checkout@v3

    # Log in to GitHub Container Registry
    - name: Log in to GHCR
      uses: docker/login-action@v2
      with:
        registry: ghcr.io
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

    # Build the Docker image
    - name: Build Docker image
      run: |
        docker build -t ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:latest .
    
    # Push the Docker image
    - name: Push Docker image
      run: |
        docker push ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:latest

    # Deploy to Kubernetes (optional)
    # Uncomment and configure if you want automatic deployment
    # - name: Deploy to K8s
    #   uses: azure/k8s-deploy@v3
    #   with:
    #     manifests: k8s/*.yaml
    #     kubeconfig: ${{ secrets.KUBE_CONFIG_DATA }}
```

> **Key points:**
> * Uses the built‑in `GITHUB_TOKEN` for authentication to GHCR.  
> * Builds and pushes the image tagged `latest`.  
> * If you want automatic deployment, set up a Kubernetes cluster and store its kubeconfig in a secret named `KUBE_CONFIG_DATA`.

---

## 4. Adding, Committing, and Pushing Changes

Once you’ve added the above files:

```bash
git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment.yaml .github/workflows/ci.yml
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and GitHub Actions workflow"
git push origin main
```

If you’re using SSH for GitHub, make sure your SSH key is added to your local agent and to GitHub.

---

### Summary

1. **Clone** the repository locally (`git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git`).  
2. **Add** the three files above.  
3. **Commit** and **push** the changes.  

Your GitHub Actions workflow will automatically build and push the Docker image whenever you push to the `main` branch. You can then deploy the new image to Kubernetes using the manifests.

Let me know if you’d like help customizing any part of these templates!
